steps.text: Shortly after the war

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: This was a resplendent place twenty-six years ago.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: At the time, the dome above was polished to a mirror sheen, and the radiance of the twin moons and the enchanting darkness of the starry sky dancing together was a most beauteous sight.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Once, I kissed the back of His Majesty's hand here. 'Paying respects to King Alistair', a rare honor indeed.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Victoria no longer has a king, my Lady—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Or should I call you the Earl of March?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Just Eleanor is fine.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: I did not beg His Grace the Duke of Normandy for the seat of County March to hold the title of Earl, but rather to expedite a few business matters, Your Highness.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: If it were not for that farcical royal hanging, we might have been much closer, Vina.
She takes out a gilded purple business card, its face embossed with nothing more than a golden loosestrife flower.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Please, take it. Since you're more accustomed to do things in a businesslike manner, this might put you at ease.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I'm afraid we are not so well-acquainted. Do you all always decide the future of Londinium here, my Lady?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: It was never up to me where we meet. Besides, considering all that's happened here, surely there is nowhere else more suited than this?
Eleanor looks at the faded statues and dusty doors at the end of the hallway, as if she could capture their past glory.
In the room beyond was the King of Victoria's throne. Upon it he once sat, dictating the rise and fall of the Empire.
But what remains behind those doors now?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: I arrived early to both walk down memory lane and to meet with you. We have much to talk about.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Did you not wish to meet me too?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You know I'm holding a—

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Vina, surely your friends from Rhodes Island have divulged what the other dukes are thinking to you.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The other dukes? I don't see much difference between you, them and the Duke of Normandy backing you.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Oh, don't get me mixed up with His Grace. He's a man worthy of respect, but it's not worth bothering him with trifles such as handling Londinium.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: As for the rest of them, I dare not say I'm worthy of comparison.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: The Sarkaz withdrawal does not mean that Londinium's troubles are over. None are willing to tally up the change in the Infected population, but the outcome is rather clear.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Victoria's pharmaceutical production lines are insufficient, and nobody wants to rework their precious factories for the sake of the Infected. You know what I mean.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: I have a long-standing partnership with the Columbian military. They've even referred me to several pharmaceutical companies.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: There is no crack that cannot be plugged. For the right price, of course.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Is that a threat?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Only if you think it is. Don't be too hasty to respond. Figure out what bargaining chips you have first before you come find me, Vina.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Let's start our future partnership on the right foot.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Oh, and, you know you can tell just by looking around that your family once steered the course of all Victoria from this ancient palace.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Your Royal Highness Alexandrina, Londinium is far too small for you—
The city's far too large, if you ask me. It shames me to admit, but the wailing I heard all across Londinium had me quaking in my boots, and in my panic, I went the wrong way.

spans.text: , if you ask me. It shames me to admit, but the wailing I heard all across Londinium had me quaking in my boots, and in my panic, I went the wrong way.

steps.text: Ah, so many tragic sights in this city...

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: You really have grown, Ellie. I still remember how you used to clamber up my back and grab onto my antlers.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: I am ever grateful for your generosity. His Grace the Duke of Normandy also reminded me that he is off soon to convalesce in greener pastures. You may join him, if you wish.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Hah, I'm not one to leave my manor before I've drained my wine cellar dry of the fine vintages within.
And here I was thinking old Normandy would understand the importance of this little meeting of ours.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: But no matter. You are the reason we have gathered here today, Alexandrina.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: *cough* Your Grace didn't need to cut to the chase quite so quickly.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: The old soldier's running late... Did he refuse your invitation again?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: He turned his eyes away from Londinium a long time ago. I'm sure your spies will have all the details of my meeting with him served to you with breakfast tomorrow.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Yet even now, his elegance is no less impressive than the time Gaul was swallowed whole.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: I wouldn't consider this a good thing for Victoria.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Tara and Dublinn... Though he has not explicitly declared independence from Victoria, only the blind fail to see the reality of the situation.

spans.text: Though he has not explicitly declared independence from Victoria, only the blind fail to see the reality of the situation.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Abercorn and Fife suffered tremendous losses, and so have 'forfeited the right' to take part in the big decisions. And the one behind Ashworth has decided to stay far from any sort of turmoil.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: As for Normandy... His stance is rather clear-cut.
Gododdin smiles at the Young Duke. Eleanor simply performs the most minute of bows in return.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Aye, the vagaries of life.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Back in those days, we still held parliamentary banquets here, and King Alistair still sat in the throne room. None would take his words lightly.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Hah.
In the dark and dusty hall, Duke Gododdin lithely taps out a beat etched in his memories with one foot, just like in days past.

Smoke, music, and the sunlight shined upon him from the dome above. He was a spirited young man back then, with all the lords and ladies at the feast lined up to be his dance partner. Even His Majesty applauded him.
Then, together with the other dukes, he sent the King to the gallows.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: No need to memorialize the dead, Your Grace. His orphan stands before us, does she not?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Hah, aye, so she does. What does it matter if Victoria has no king?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: The Siege. That's all I can call you until you accept our proposal.

spans.text: That's all I can call you until you accept our proposal.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: There are better ways to implement your ideas on the Infected, the refugees, even those pain-in-the-arse Sarkaz.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: ...Madam Speaker.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Should I consider this advice from the 'will of the empire'?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Call it an attempt at giving some. We have other means to handle this near-ruined city.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: This is not a lifetime appointment. We will judge whether or not you are fit for the position.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Just like the past, no?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: With your 'dinner table Parliament', a handful of dukes could dance around the King behind closed doors, deciding the nation's future on a whim.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: And the results? Look outside. We have not yet washed ourselves clean of all the Sarkaz blood—

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: You look only at this little city, while I look at the whole of Victoria.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: If Londinium has become an ulcer sapping Victoria's strength, I do not mind gouging it out.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I will allow other nations to see Victoria bleed, but I will not tolerate them mocking our scars, nauseating though they may be.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: If you stand in a sewer, you cannot expect to have full view of an ancient empire. Do not forget that the family name 'Victoria' is no stranger to me, Your Royal Highness Alexandrina.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Only the strong and the heroic have the power to steer the empire on its future course.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Let's not frighten our future friend, Your Grace. Didn't we gather here to soothe our worries in a more pleasant manner?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Old Wellington is far from the core, Windermere is in a constant state of uproar, and the rest are keeping an eye on how we stand.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Since it's rare for us all to see eye-to-eye on a matter, let's keep things simple.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: That, I cannot deny. But Vina, you can do far more than this.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Though this does not mean the Speaker must sit on the throne, Ellie.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Are you all finished?
She draws her sword, and the hall falls deathly silent.

a.text: Vina insisted on recording some minutes for that secret meeting.

spans.text: Vina insisted on recording some minutes for that secret meeting.

a.text: It was a meeting to decide Londinium's future, so her residents had the right to know what happened exactly.

spans.text: It was a meeting to decide Londinium's future, so her residents had the right to know what happened exactly.

a.text: I stood there in my hiding spot, trying to note down every word as impartially as I could, but when I saw Vina draw that sword from her hip, pointing it at those bastards who thought they knew it all...

spans.text: I stood there in my hiding spot, trying to note down every word as impartially as I could, but when I saw Vina draw that sword from her hip, pointing it at those bastards who thought they knew it all...

a.text: I hoped from my deepest heart that she would strike them all down. That way, what came next might have gone differently.

spans.text: I hoped from my deepest heart that she would strike them all down. That way, what came next might have gone differently.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: My teacher once told me the Sighs of Kings was used to behead rebellious nobles—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No, not the Sighs of Kings any longer, though I do not know what to call it now.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I have not the right to name it, as it was the workers who forged it. To commemorate that victory, whose painful sting has not yet left us.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: At first, as it lay forgotten upon the muddy battlefield, I thought its duty had ended.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But those heroes who lost everything still remember it, because it symbolizes the Victoria held in their hearts. They do not wish to see her laden with dust once more.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I know what they intended when they gave it to me. They wanted me to judge in their stead... Judge those who brought them to desolation and ruin.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But you don't fear it, do you?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: It was never the sword you feared.
Vina gently caresses the flourishes on both sides of the sword's crossguard, every detail sculpted by the artisans of Londinium.
A hammer and a sword. They glimmer in the darkness.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: 'So long as the sword gleams, Victoria's honor will shine eternal.'

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: They begged my aid in reforging this sword, broken to the point of no return... using my hammer as its core.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Once reforged, they offered it to me without hesitation. But at the time, I could make no promises. King? Speaker? As far as I'm concerned...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Neither title is worth a damn. I'm no different from them. I'm just a woman who wanted to go home.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: And when I made it back, what did I find?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I didn't see the 'grand' Victoria you do.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But I did see Infected children in the boxing gym, hoping to learn pugilism so they could defend their homes. And drunkards, mouths full of rotting teeth, donating the drinks they had stashed away to the hospitals, all so soldiers on the operating table could be saved.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The glory of empire has long since left us, so far in the distance it can no longer warm our hard beds in the winter chill of the new year.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: This sword is the duty they entrusted to me. I need neither Parliament nor royal authority to know what I must do.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I will do what I can to show them the power they hold in their hands. To make them understand the land is theirs to protect!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But until that day comes, I must stand at their forefront, no matter what title I bear.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Sewers too, may bloom. And so, here, in my home...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I will NOT be lectured by the likes of you!
Vina firmly plants the sword into the ground, its point passing through the stone like butter. It stands tall before the dukes.
All eyes fall upon the quivering sword. A very clear provocation from Vina.
'Realmblade' and 'miracle'. In the wake of the war, those two words have become joined at the hip.
Rather than 'the late king's orphan', they are much more concerned about Vina's other identity.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Hah, well said, my Lady! There's really no point in us keeping the sword nowadays.

spans.text: Hah, well said, my Lady! There's really no point in

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Best you pull it right out, no point in nicking such a fine blade.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Your teacher really did give you a practical education. It seems we were worried over nothing, Duke Caster.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Indeed. A rather childish way of doing things, but one that will win over the people. Parliament will see her mature faster than ever.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Wait just a bloody minute—

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: We have no choice, Siege. Sundered Victoria needs a new voice, and you have stepped forward.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: But I have seen many die by their own blades, leading me to think long and hard about taking up that particular one.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Do not let it cut you, Madam Speaker. That is my advice.

options: She's more clear-headed than Your Graces think.
I'd say you've done pretty well so far, Vina.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Doctor?!

steps.name: Trilby Asher
steps.text: Pardon me, Your Grace. We were... unable to stop the Doctor.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Bored growl)

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: You are dismissed.

options: Londinium needs a leader who can protect everyone.
You cannot rely on anyone else.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Doctor...

options: The final decision is yours, naturally.
We will do everything we can to help the Infected here.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: How interesting. A pharmaceutical company specialized in Oripathy that often dips its toe into areas outside its expertise.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: You circumvented the ducal alliance, and tendered a ceasefire with those Sarkaz.

options: Well, there was no reaction from Your Graces' fleets.
You assented to it, did you not?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Merely a gift, as thanks for all you have done on the battlefield.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: There are some lines that must not be crossed.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: We will await your answer, Siege.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: As for Rhodes Island, you lot have been keeping quiet for a while now. Why the sudden urgency?

options: Time itself makes for irrational decisions.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Oh? Time, is it...?

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: Vina, have a good think about what the people you're still protecting really need.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: And remember, if you do make your decision, don't get too close with those Rhodes Islanders.

options: I believe we have a good relationship with Duke of Normandy, my Lady.

steps.name: The Young Duke
steps.text: That's exactly why I'm warning Vina, 'Doctor' of Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: She's not quite like the other dukes.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: So, what should we do now, Doctor?

options: You already have your answer, don't you, Vina?
It's not good for Rhodes to get more involved in Londinium's affairs.
Most of our staff... will withdraw from Londinium ASAP.

steps.name: Longshot
steps.text: It's been a long time since Babel took my brothers away. As for us who stayed, it's been real rough lately.

steps.name: Longshot
steps.text: Hmph. Just do it already. I've got nothing else to say.
He looks all around him, watching the people on their benches whisper to one another uneasily, an unconscious sneer on his face.
This place fettered him, and in its magnanimity, it had also fettered those who would decide his fate.
Not too long ago, Vina vetoed a proposal to use the Palace of Westhaleg to house the Parliament, instead choosing this building oft rented out by the royal family.
She hoped this would be the starting point of a new Parliament.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I've finished looking into him, Vina.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Longshot, a lifelong mercenary, hails from a place in Kazdel called the Scar Market. During the war, he took part in defending the city in the name of the Military Commission. He never saw the front lines.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Two months ago, Babel organized a withdrawal effort. He didn't follow them. Instead, he got captured by Indra and Dagda while covering for some local Sarkaz as they evacuated. You really did save him.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I... don't remember that.

steps.name: Longshot
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: After he committed this latest crime of his, we followed his trail and found the people he was hiding.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: His daughter has been helping a few Sarkaz leave the city these past two months. But this time she's part of the group sneaking out herself.

steps.name: Longshot
steps.text: *Sarkaz expletive*!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You attacked the shopkeep who recognized you for supplies, didn't you?

steps.name: Longshot
steps.text: Aaaaaghhh—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Restrain him!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Don't lose your temper just yet, Longshot. Your loved ones managed to slip through our fingers. Someone's helping them.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Millscar. Sounds familiar, right?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Their 'business' is creeping into places they shouldn't be creeping into.

steps.name: Longshot
steps.text: ...Hah. Haha.

steps.name: Longshot
steps.text: I don't know a damned thing, Feline. Just kill me already.

steps.name: Longshot
steps.text: Worried my blood's going to get this pretty little place all dirty?

steps.name: Longshot
steps.text: The war's just ended, and you're already trembling at the sight of some red?!

steps.name: Longshot
steps.text: None of you sitting here have even one-tenth of the honesty of those Sarkaz you refuse to call Victorians!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Just leave the rest to me.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Hoarse Voice
steps.text: Any new instructions from Her Grace on the latest going-ons in the city?

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: Her Grace has long since been aware of the trouble these Sarkaz and this Millscar have been causing, and she is very concerned about the safety of the citizens.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: But now Parliament is fully assembled, and since the Speaker has been doing a fine job of solving the issues plaguing the citizenry, she believes things will improve.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: However...

steps.name: Hoarse Voice
steps.text: However?

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: When it comes to rooting out the risks against Londinium's safety, Her Grace is of the opinion that we should not tarry, especially in regards to Millscar.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: And so, there are still problems in this city that we must urge the Speaker to resolve sooner rather than later.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Boss, Parliament hanged that devil, but we managed to snag the stuff he left for us.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: These goods...

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Send them out.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: But boss... That's way too risky right now. Parliament's been trying to sniff us out 24/7.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Then hide them for a spell. They've paid their due, so we'll get them delivered. No need to worry about anything else.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Nobody knows about this batch anyway, maybe we can just—
The mercenary gestures at his neck, but a sharp pain accompanied by a chill suddenly prickles at his chin.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: B-Boss, I had to say it, even if you kill me! That's the best way to handle things!

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Didn't those devils kill a whole bunch of our people?!

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: If you really cared, you'd be on the Exemplars' list of decommissioned soldiers, not here.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: But there's nothing wrong with caution, I suppose. With the new Speaker so concerned about the city's safety, we're an inevitable target alongside the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Impatient Mercenary
steps.text: Hmph. Those devils brought it upon themselves, though.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Two months ago, they decided not to withdraw alongside the rest of their kin. Now that things are heading south for them and they finally wish to flee, it's natural they have to pay extra.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Don't worry. If this goes well, more and more business opportunities will be coming our way.

steps.name: Discharged Female Soldier
steps.text: You're back. How'd it go? Did you manage to get any?

steps.name: Injured Exemplar
steps.text: Sanatorium's as full as a tin of fins. Everyone's trying to get their suppressant as soon as they can, not to mention what just happened to Madam Major...

steps.name: Injured Exemplar
steps.text: Sorry, Diane. Not even Exemplars get special treatment.

steps.name: Injured Exemplar
steps.text: Rhodes Island's been working around the clock to provide as many suppressants as they can, but there's just too many new Infected—

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I... I understand.

steps.name: Injured Exemplar
steps.text: Hmm... Well, it's not like we've got no way of getting any. I've heard from some war buddies that there's private channels...

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Illegal ones?

steps.name: Injured Exemplar
steps.text: Hey, as long as you live to see another day—
There's other means of buying medicine? Huh. My boss never told me we'd have competitors.

steps.name: Injured Exemplar
steps.text: Hmph. Sure you didn't hear me wrong, mister?
Ah, sorry, my trip from Columbia must have tired me out too much. Hello, I'm Eliseo. Here, my business card.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Colum...bia? Pure Heart Medical?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: That's right, I rushed over to Victoria to find... to find...

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Err, one second, let me check my list...

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Ever since I arrived in Londinium, nearly everything's been different to how the preliminary briefing described it.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Found it. Londinium's interim health secretary... Madam Major. Could you tell me how to get to the Office of Provisional Supply Procurement?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Rest assured, I'm here representing Pure Heart Medical to discuss medical cooperation. The situation here will get better soon.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Did I... say something wrong?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Didn't you hear the news? Madam Major has... passed away. Just this morning.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Sorry.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Sorry, I lost my cool for a second. No matter how hard we must strive, Pure Heart Medical's sincerity and dedication will not change.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: But right now, could you please take me to her office?
